html:
The Austrian Empire was the name taken in 1804 by the lands of the Habsburgs: Austria, Bohemia, Hungary and much else in central Europe, ruled from Vienna. The map uses the label from 1650 onward, for the Habsburg Monarchy that came before it.

The Habsburgs gained Bohemia and Hungary after the Battle of Mohács in 1526. In 1683 they beat the Ottomans at the Battle of Vienna and by 1699 had taken all of Hungary. The War of the Spanish Succession added the southern Netherlands, Milan and Naples. Maria Theresa, from 1740, lost Silesia to Prussia but held the rest, and her son Joseph II pushed hard reforms from the centre.

When Napoleon crowned himself emperor, Francis II answered by proclaiming the Austrian Empire in 1804, and in 1806 he ended the Holy Roman Empire. After Napoleon's fall, Vienna hosted the Congress of Vienna in 1815, and the chancellor Metternich made the empire the guardian of the old order. The revolutions of 1848 almost broke it. Defeat by Prussia in 1866 led to the compromise of 1867 that turned it into Austria-Hungary.
